back: The next best alternative forgone (given up) when a choice is made.

front: Why does every choice have an opportunity cost?
back: Because resources are scarce and have alternative uses: using them one way means not using them another.

front: Is opportunity cost all the alternatives given up?
back: No. It is only the next best (second-ranked) alternative.

front: Does a free event have an opportunity cost?
back: Yes. The time and resources used could have been used for the next best alternative.

front: How do you find the opportunity cost of one unit of good X in terms of good Y?
back: Units of Y given up ÷ units of X gained.

front: Opportunity cost of studying full-time for a worker?
back: The wages (and work experience) given up while studying.

front: How does opportunity cost help a government?
back: It shows what each project gives up (for example a hospital instead of a dam), so the benefits of alternatives can be compared.

front: What steps find the opportunity cost of a choice?
back: List the alternatives, rank them, take the first choice; the opportunity cost is the second-ranked alternative.

front: Is the money price of a good its opportunity cost?
back: No. Opportunity cost is the alternative given up, not the price paid.
